title: Building sets with an organized band and the Broadwater Hotel
summary: DeDroit contrasts his organized sets with a pickup band he sent to the Broadwater Hotel in Biloxi and quotes a bad review.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh, in the forties, in the forties, up to fifty-nine. We used as many men as we could. We tried to engage those men for the whole season. So you'd be sure you have them. You'd give them all the dates, and I'd make them sign it, but they accepted the dates. See? Then you have, by the time after you play one or two balls, you've got an organized orchestra, because they're good musicians. And they save you a lot of trouble. You don't do a lot of talking. They know what you're going to do, you know what I mean? And that's a great thing. But case in point, I never would take a steady job after I left the setting, you see. And the Broadwater Hotel used to hire good orchestras over in Biloxi. And the manager asked me to play with it, and I couldn't. I didn't want to. So one time he said, Johnny, my band's one day late, I don't have a band. And he sent me a band, and I sent him a pickup band from the union. So next time I went there myself. And he says, I want to tell you something. He says, you know that band you sent over here? He says, I just had to tell them. He says, I went up and told them, you fellas have never played a job in your life together. That was the truth. He says, every time you play a set you have a union meeting. What are you going to play? He says, Johnny comes here, he says his manager puts the lights on, puts the music racks, he walks out on the band's tent and says how to do folks and starts. And he says, I have a little word. I call out the numbers. There's no discussion, let's play this and let's play that. An organized band doesn't play like that. You don't have that in there. You build your sets. You start, you play to a climax if you're going to play. You want to finish. And when I'd say, that's all, that was my, when I'd say that's all, in fact they used to pick it up in the newspaper, they said, you'll have a good time until Johnny says that's all. You know what I did a little? I'd show you some write-ups from here that said, with the exception of my trumpet playing, there was nothing in the show at the off, he was married. But that's how the guy wrote up the show. With the exception of Johnny's trumpet playing, there's nothing of merit in the show. And there's eight acts including Jack Benny and all of them. The guy must have loved me. I wasn't lucky.
